title: Cedar Plank Grilled Salmon
seoTitle: Cedar Plank Grilled Salmon | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Smoke-kissed salmon without the mess
description: Smoke-kissed salmon without the mess. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Cedar Plank Grilled Salmon in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Soy sauce, Fresh ginger, grated as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch seafood. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Soak plank and prep fish
steps.instruction: Soak cedar plank 1 hour. Pat salmon dry. Mix glaze. Score skin lightly so it doesn't curl. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Grill on the plank
steps.instruction: Grill indirect at 375°F on the plank 12–18 minutes until salmon flakes at 125–130°F in the thickest part (medium). Skin may stick — that's fine; serve flesh side up. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Glaze and serve
steps.instruction: Brush glaze in the last 3 minutes. Rest 2 minutes. Serve from plank or transfer with a wide spatula. Hold backup fillets at 160°F max — salmon toughens fast.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for fish, 145°F for shrimp until opaque. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Cedar Plank Grilled Salmon onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Portion for the hall
steps.instruction: Break fillets into portions on trays. Keep skin on for transport — crew can peel if they want. Do not cover tightly or fish steams.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Cedar Plank Grilled Salmon — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Rest grilled proteins 5–8 minutes under foil before slicing — juices stay in the meat.
tonightSpread: Plate Cedar Plank Grilled Salmon with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Cedar Plank Grilled Salmon on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
Slice proteins on a cutting board at the end of the line so everyone sees the smoke ring and char.
Set sauce and pickles on the side — sauced meat holds better on the backup tray.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Slice cold protein thin for next-day wraps or salads — faster reheat, less dry-out.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Smoke-kissed salmon without the mess. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Frozen shrimp is fine — thaw under cold running water and pat very dry.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Cedar Plank Grilled Salmon runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
